title: Understanding LONI
subtitle: What LONI is and why your role matters.

sections.title: What LONI is
sections.body: LONI is a maternal support platform. It gives mothers AI pregnancy guidance, access to nurses through voice calls, and emergency transportation when they need to get to care quickly.

sections.title: The Driver's role
sections.body: As a LONI Driver, you provide safe, calm emergency transportation. You receive a request, pick up the mother, and take her to her selected or assigned hospital.

sections.title: Why safe transportation matters
sections.body: A mother in an emergency relies on you. Calm, careful driving and respectful support can make a real difference to her safety and wellbeing.

title: Basic Rules of Safe Driving
subtitle: The habits that keep every trip safe.

sections.title: Defensive driving
sections.body: Anticipate hazards before they happen. Keep a safe following distance and always be ready to react.

sections.title: Speed awareness
sections.body: Respect speed limits and slow down near hospitals, schools, and busy areas. Arriving safely matters more than arriving fast.

sections.title: Seatbelts
sections.body: Wear your seatbelt at all times and make sure every passenger is buckled before you move.

sections.title: Avoid distractions
sections.body: Do not use your phone while driving. Set navigation before you move and pull over safely if you need to adjust it.

sections.title: Difficult weather
sections.body: In rain or poor visibility, reduce speed, increase following distance, and use your lights.

title: Supporting a Mother
subtitle: How to care for a mother respectfully.

sections.title: Treat mothers respectfully
sections.body: Speak kindly and give the mother space. Ask before helping and never rush her.

sections.title: Protect privacy
sections.body: Never share a mother's name, destination, or situation with anyone else. What happens on a trip stays private.

sections.title: Communicate calmly
sections.body: A calm voice helps a worried mother feel safe. Explain what you're doing in simple, reassuring words.

sections.title: Help her enter and exit
sections.body: Open the door and offer a steady hand or arm if needed. Be patient and let her move at her own pace.

sections.title: What you should and should not do
sections.body: You are NOT a medical professional. Do not diagnose, treat, or give medical advice. Your job is safe, calm transport - if a mother needs medical help, get her to care and alert support.

title: How to Pick Up a Mother
subtitle: The exact LONI pickup flow, step by step.

sections.title: The flow
sections.body: Request received -> Accept request -> Navigate to pickup -> Arrive -> Confirm mother -> Start trip.

sections.title: Navigate to pickup
sections.body: Start navigation as soon as you accept. Share your ETA so the mother knows when to expect you.

sections.title: Arrive
sections.body: Pull up safely at the pickup point and mark that you've arrived.

sections.title: Confirm the mother
sections.body: Before she gets in, confirm you have the right passenger. Gently ask her name and match it to the request. This prevents picking up the wrong person.

sections.title: Start the trip
sections.body: Only start the trip once the mother is safely seated and buckled in.

title: Payments, Safety & LONI's No-Tip Policy
subtitle: Safety comes first. Your safety and the mother's safety come before completing a trip. LONI handles the mother's payment. Learn what you must never ask for, and how to report payment issues.

sections.title: Your Safety
bullets: Never speed because a trip is marked as an emergency.
Never use a phone while driving unless using a safe hands-free method.
Ensure the mother has access to a seatbelt where applicable.
Never drive when tired, impaired, or unable to drive safely.
Do not allow unsafe passengers or situations.
If continuing the trip would put anyone in immediate danger, prioritize safety and contact LONI.

sections.title: When Something Goes Wrong
sections.body: Report issues through LONI rather than trying to resolve serious problems yourself.
sections.note: You are not a medical professional. If the mother appears to require medical attention, follow LONI's emergency procedure and contact emergency support - do not attempt treatment.

sections.title: How Payment Works
sections.body: You don't need to collect payment from the mother. LONI manages the payment process.
sections.note: Remain professional regardless of whether a mother offers a tip. If LONI's policy does not support tips, politely decline.
